Catalase-positive organisms like Aspergillus can break down Hâ‚‚Oâ‚‚, so they particularly thrive when the oxidative burst is already impaired, as in CGD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CVID involves B cell dysfunction and low immunoglobulin levels, predisposing to encapsulated bacterial infections, not specifically catalase-positive fungal infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (Bruton's) involves absent B cells and immunoglobulins, predisposing to encapsulated bacteria, not specifically Aspergillus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: DiGeorge syndrome involves T cell deficiency from thymic aplasia. While T cell deficiency increases infection risk, the specific vulnerability to catalase-positive organisms is CGD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Selective IgA deficiency primarily increases mucosal infections and may predispose to Giardia, not specifically Aspergillus.

questions.stem: A patient with PCP has a dry, nonproductive cough making sputum collection difficult. Which of the following procedures is most likely to obtain an adequate sample for diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Most PCP patients have a dry, nonproductive cough, making sputum collection difficult. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) has a much better chance of obtaining an adequate sample for silver stain, PCR, or fluorescent antibody testing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most patients with PCP have a dry, unproductive cough, so getting a good sputum sample is difficult. Bronchoscopy with BAL has a much better chance of obtaining an adequate sample for diagnostic testing (silver stain, Giemsa, immunofluorescent staining, or PCR). BAL allows direct sampling of alveolar fluid where P. jirovecii cysts and trophozoites reside.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nasopharyngeal swabs sample the upper airway and would not adequately capture P. jirovecii from the lower respiratory tract.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Induced sputum can sometimes be used for PCP diagnosis, but BAL from bronchoscopy is more reliable and has higher sensitivity, especially when cough is nonproductive.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Throat swab cultures would not detect P. jirovecii, which infects the lower respiratory tract and does not grow on standard culture media.
whyWrongByChoice.E: P. jirovecii does not grow on standard fungal culture media (including Sabouraud agar) and does not typically cause bloodstream infections. Blood culture would be uninformative.

questions.stem: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) develops in patients with which of the following pre-existing conditions?

explanation.summary: CPA develops in patients with pre-existing structural lung disease (healed TB cavities, COPD, sarcoidosis) over months to years. It involves chronic colonization of abnormal lung spaces rather than tissue invasion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis is a group of slowly progressive disorders in patients with pre-existing structural lung disease (e.g., healed tuberculosis cavities, COPD, sarcoidosis). CPA develops over months to years and involves chronic colonization of abnormal lung spaces rather than tissue invasion. Diagnosis is supported by elevated Aspergillus-specific IgG.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Well-controlled asthma is not the typical setting for CPA. ABPA occurs in asthmatics. CPA requires structural lung disease with pre-existing cavities or damage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acute neutropenia from chemotherapy predisposes to invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA), not the slowly progressive chronic form.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HIV with low CD4 predisposes to PCP, not typically CPA. CPA requires structural lung damage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DKA predisposes to mucormycosis, not chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following antibody tests is most useful for diagnosing ABPA versus CPA/aspergilloma?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspergillus IgE for ABPA; IgG for CPA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aspergillus IgM for ABPA; IgA for CPA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both tests are negative in these conditions

explanation.summary: Aspergillus-specific IgE is elevated in ABPA (driven by Th2/type I hypersensitivity), while Aspergillus-specific IgG is elevated in CPA/aspergilloma (chronic colonization/infection). Neither antibody test is useful for IPA because immunosuppressed patients cannot mount reliable antibody responses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillus-specific IgE is used to diagnose ABPA, where a Th2-mediated hypersensitivity response drives elevated IgE levels. Aspergillus-specific IgG is used to diagnose CPA or aspergilloma, which involve chronic colonization or infection triggering a different immune response. Importantly, neither IgE nor IgG is useful for diagnosing invasive aspergillosis, where immunosuppressed patients cannot mount reliable antibody responses.

whyWrongByChoice.B: While IgG may also be elevated in ABPA, the key distinguishing test for ABPA is elevated IgE. CPA is specifically diagnosed with IgG, not IgE.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgM and IgA are not the standard antibody markers used to distinguish ABPA from CPA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antibody tests are positive in both conditionsâ€”IgE in ABPA and IgG in CPA. They are negative/unreliable only in IPA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Galactomannan antigen testing is used for invasive aspergillosis, not for distinguishing ABPA from CPA.

questions.stem: The first-line treatment for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia is which of the following?

explanation.summary: TMP-SMX is the first-line treatment for PCP. It inhibits folate synthesis. Second-line alternatives include pentamidine, atovaquone, or clindamycin plus primaquine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) is first-line for both treatment and prophylaxis of PCP. It works by inhibiting sequential steps in folate synthesis. Second-line alternatives include pentamidine, atovaquone, or clindamycin plus primaquine for patients who cannot tolerate TMP-SMX.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Voriconazole is first-line for invasive aspergillosis. P. jirovecii lacks ergosterol, making azole antifungals ineffective.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Amphotericin B targets ergosterol in fungal membranes. Since P. jirovecii lacks ergosterol, amphotericin B is ineffective.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Caspofungin targets Î²-D-glucan synthesis. While P. jirovecii has Î²-D-glucan, echinocandins are not standard treatment for PCP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fluconazole targets ergosterol synthesis. Since P. jirovecii lacks ergosterol, fluconazole is ineffective.

questions.stem: Which of the following patient populations is at highest risk for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neonates with Group B Strep colonization

explanation.summary: IPA most commonly occurs in patients with prolonged neutropenia, hematologic malignancy, high-dose corticosteroids, or other severe immunosuppression. Neutrophils provide the primary defense against Aspergillus in immunocompetent individuals.
explanation.whyCorrect: IPA most often occurs in patients with prolonged neutropenia or neutrophil dysfunction, hematologic malignancy, high-dose corticosteroids, or other immunosuppressive therapies. Neutrophils provide effective defense against Aspergillus in immunocompetent individuals, so neutropenia dramatically increases IPA risk. Additional risk factors include transplantation, advanced HIV, and CGD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Well-controlled asthmatics may develop ABPA (a non-invasive allergic condition) but are not at high risk for invasive aspergillosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Healthy adults inhale Aspergillus conidia daily but rarely develop invasive disease because intact neutrophil function controls the organism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neonates with GBS colonization are at risk for GBS pneumonia/sepsis, not invasive aspergillosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Elderly patients with hypertension alone are not at significantly increased risk for IPA without immunosuppression.

questions.stem: PCR testing for P. jirovecii has excellent sensitivity but a key limitation. Which of the following best describes this limitation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PCR cannot detect P. jirovecii DNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: PCR cannot distinguish exposure from active infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: PCR requires tissue biopsy and cannot use BAL

choices.label: D
choices.text: PCR is only available at reference laboratories

choices.label: E
choices.text: PCR has high specificity but poor sensitivity

explanation.summary: PCR has excellent sensitivity for detecting P. jirovecii but cannot distinguish between environmental exposure/colonization and active infection. People are exposed to P. jirovecii daily and may have detectable DNA without disease. PCR is typically paired with other methods for confirmation.
explanation.whyCorrect: PCR has excellent sensitivity for detecting P. jirovecii DNA, but this is also its greatest weakness. People are exposed to P. jirovecii daily and breathe the fungus into their lungs. There is also evidence of pulmonary colonization. Because of this, PCR cannot distinguish between someone who simply breathed in the organism (exposure/colonization) and those with active infection. PCR is typically paired with staining or other diagnostic methods for confirmation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PCR can detect P. jirovecii DNA with excellent sensitivity. Detection is not the problemâ€”distinguishing colonization from disease is.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PCR can be performed on BAL fluid, induced sputum, or other respiratory specimens. Tissue biopsy is not required.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PCR for P. jirovecii is available at many clinical laboratories, not just reference labs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The opposite is trueâ€”PCR has excellent sensitivity but specificity is limited because it cannot differentiate colonization from infection.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia is on day 18 of induction chemotherapy. His absolute neutrophil count is 120 cells/uL. He develops fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hemoptysis. Chest CT reveals a pulmonary nodule surrounded by ground-glass opacity. Serum galactomannan is positive. Which morphology is expected on biopsy?

explanation.summary: Neutropenia + halo sign + positive galactomannan = invasive aspergillosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillus hyphae are septate with acute-angle (approximately 45 degrees) branching. Galactomannan is a cell wall component of Aspergillus, and the halo sign reflects hemorrhage around angioinvasive fungal lesions in neutropenic hosts.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Broad non-septate hyphae with ~90 degree branching characterize Mucorales, not Aspergillus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Encapsulated yeast describes Cryptococcus, which does not produce galactomannan.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Helmet-shaped cysts describe Pneumocystis jirovecii on silver stain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudohyphae with blastoconidia describe Candida species.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes presents with diabetic ketoacidosis, facial pain, and a black eschar on the hard palate. Biopsy is pending but imaging shows sinus opacification with extension into the orbit. Which intervention should be initiated immediately?

choices.label: B
choices.text: IV amphotericin B plus surgical debridement

explanation.summary: DKA + black eschar = rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis; urgent amphotericin B plus debridement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucormycosis is angioinvasive and rapidly progressive. First-line therapy is amphotericin B combined with aggressive surgical debridement, and treatment should not wait for laboratory confirmation when clinical suspicion is high.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Voriconazole is first-line for invasive aspergillosis but is NOT active against Mucorales.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Itraconazole has insufficient activity against Mucorales and is not appropriate as monotherapy for life-threatening invasive disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Echinocandins such as caspofungin have no meaningful activity against Mucorales.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Delay is catastrophic; mortality is 50-80% and therapy must begin empirically.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 85 cells/uL) who is non-adherent to therapy presents with 3 weeks of progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and low-grade fever. Chest CT shows diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities. Which diagnostic finding is most specific for the likely organism?

explanation.summary: Advanced HIV + ground-glass opacities = Pneumocystis jirovecii; silver stain shows indented, helmet-shaped cysts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pneumocystis does not grow on standard fungal media, so diagnosis relies on visualization of cysts using methenamine silver stain, which reveals characteristic indented helmet-shaped forms, or PCR/direct fluorescent antibody of BAL.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Galactomannan detects Aspergillus cell wall components, not Pneumocystis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pneumocystis cannot be cultured; it lacks ergosterol and does not grow on standard fungal media.
whyWrongByChoice.D: India ink demonstrates cryptococcal capsule in CSF, a different opportunistic organism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Non-septate hyphae describe Mucorales, not Pneumocystis.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis has worsening asthma-like symptoms, expectoration of brown mucus plugs, and central bronchiectasis on CT. Labs show eosinophilia and markedly elevated total IgE with positive Aspergillus-specific IgE and IgG. Which mechanism best explains her disease?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type I and III hypersensitivity to colonizing fungus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cytotoxic T-cell destruction of infected cells

explanation.summary: ABPA = type I (IgE) + type III (immune complex) hypersensitivity to airway Aspergillus colonization in asthma/CF.
explanation.whyCorrect: ABPA results from colonization of airways by Aspergillus in patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis, triggering IgE-mediated (type I) and immune-complex-mediated (type III) hypersensitivity, yielding eosinophilia, elevated IgE, and central bronchiectasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Angioinvasion describes invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in immunocompromised hosts, not ABPA.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulomatous/Th1-mediated disease characterizes hypersensitivity pneumonitis (type IV), which is a different Aspergillus-associated process.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complement does not directly lyse Aspergillus; ABPA is not complement-mediated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD8 cytotoxic responses do not drive ABPA.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with a history of healed pulmonary tuberculosis and a residual upper lobe cavity develops hemoptysis. CT shows a rounded mass within the old cavity that moves with patient positioning. He is not immunosuppressed. What is the most appropriate management for symptomatic disease?

explanation.summary: Fungus ball (aspergilloma) in a pre-existing cavity with hemoptysis requires surgical removal plus antifungals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aspergillomas form within pre-existing cavities (commonly from prior TB). Symptomatic disease, especially with hemoptysis, requires surgical resection because the fungal mass cannot be eradicated by antifungal therapy alone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: TMP-SMX targets Pneumocystis, not Aspergillus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Corticosteroids treat ABPA, not aspergilloma, and would worsen invasive disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TB is healed; there is no evidence of active mycobacterial infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Symptomatic aspergilloma with hemoptysis carries major bleeding risk; intervention is indicated.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman hospitalized for severe COVID-19 received several weeks of high-dose dexamethasone. She has poorly controlled type 2 diabetes. Three weeks later she presents with periorbital edema, ophthalmoplegia, and facial numbness. Which pathophysiologic feature best explains her susceptibility?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated free iron and ketone reductase activity

explanation.summary: Mucorales thrive in acidic, high-glucose, iron-rich environments of DKA plus steroid immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucorales organisms possess ketone reductase and grow well in acidic, high-glucose environments. Acidosis reduces transferrin iron binding, increasing free iron that further enhances fungal proliferation; steroids compound susceptibility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: NADPH oxidase defects (CGD) predispose to Aspergillus, not specifically Mucorales.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD4 depletion is the key risk for Pneumocystis and cryptococcus, not mucormycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MAC complement deficiency predisposes to Neisseria, not fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.E: B-cell dysfunction predisposes to encapsulated bacteria, not Mucorales.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy with recurrent bacterial and fungal infections is diagnosed with chronic granulomatous disease (CGD). He develops fever and a pulmonary nodule with halo sign. Which property of the likely organism makes CGD patients especially vulnerable?

explanation.summary: Aspergillus is catalase-positive; CGD patients with defective NADPH oxidase cannot clear catalase-producing organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: CGD is characterized by defective NADPH oxidase and failure to generate reactive oxygen species. Catalase-positive organisms like Aspergillus destroy their own peroxide, leaving CGD phagocytes without weapon, yielding invasive disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus is not encapsulated; Cryptococcus is.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgA protease is a virulence factor of certain bacteria (e.g., Neisseria), not Aspergillus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aspergillus contains ergosterol; this is how azoles and amphotericin target it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Protein A is a Staphylococcus aureus virulence factor.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with a prior post-tuberculous cavity develops chronic cough, weight loss, and night sweats over 8 months. Chest CT shows a cavitary lesion with peripheral thickening, and serum Aspergillus-specific IgG is markedly elevated. Hematogenous spread is absent. What is the most appropriate first-line therapy?

explanation.summary: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis with elevated Aspergillus IgG: long-term oral itraconazole or voriconazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: CPA is a slowly progressive disease in patients with structural lung disease, diagnosed by elevated Aspergillus-specific IgG. First-line is long-term oral itraconazole or voriconazole; amphotericin is reserved for severe disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Amphotericin B is second-line, reserved for severe or refractory CPA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Corticosteroids treat ABPA and would worsen colonization in CPA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TMP-SMX targets Pneumocystis, not Aspergillus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgery alone is not first-line; medical therapy is the cornerstone of CPA management.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old allogeneic stem cell transplant recipient develops fever and pulmonary nodules. Serum galactomannan is negative, serum beta-D-glucan is negative, and biopsy shows broad ribbon-like non-septate hyphae with right-angle branching. Which therapy is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: Negative galactomannan and beta-D-glucan with ribbon-like non-septate right-angle hyphae = Mucorales; treat with amphotericin B.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucorales lack galactomannan and beta-D-glucan in their cell walls, so both tests will be negative. Broad non-septate hyphae with right-angle (~90 degrees) branching confirms mucormycosis, treated with amphotericin B.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Voriconazole treats Aspergillus but is ineffective against Mucorales.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluconazole does not cover Aspergillus or Mucorales.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Echinocandins target beta-D-glucan synthesis; Mucorales lack beta-D-glucan and are not susceptible.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TMP-SMX treats Pneumocystis, not Mucorales.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman with newly diagnosed HIV has a CD4 count of 180 cells/uL and no active pulmonary symptoms. She is starting antiretroviral therapy. What additional intervention is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: CD4 <200 in HIV: start TMP-SMX prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii.
explanation.whyCorrect: PCP prophylaxis with TMP-SMX is indicated in HIV patients once CD4 falls below 200 cells/uL. Widespread use of this prophylaxis is why PCP incidence has declined dramatically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Voriconazole prophylaxis is not standard in HIV without hematologic malignancy/transplant.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amphotericin is not used for routine fungal prophylaxis in HIV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Galactomannan surveillance is used in high-risk hematologic patients, not routine HIV care.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhaled steroids treat asthma, not opportunistic infections.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with granulomatosis with polyangiitis on high-dose prednisone and cyclophosphamide develops subacute dyspnea and dry cough. Chest CT shows diffuse ground-glass opacities. BAL PCR for Pneumocystis is positive; silver stain shows cysts. Which feature of this organism explains why culture was not attempted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It forms pseudohyphae only in vivo

choices.label: D
choices.text: It produces lethal aflatoxins in culture

choices.label: E
choices.text: It lacks ergosterol and fails to grow on media

explanation.summary: Pneumocystis jirovecii lacks ergosterol and does not grow on standard fungal media; diagnosis is by stain/PCR/DFA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pneumocystis is an atypical fungus lacking ergosterol in its cell membrane; it cannot be cultured on standard fungal media. Diagnosis depends on visualization via silver stain, PCR, or direct fluorescent antibody of BAL samples.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pneumocystis exists as trophozoites and cysts, not pseudohyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pneumocystis does not require anaerobic conditions; it simply cannot be cultured.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pneumocystis is not obligately intracellular.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aflatoxin production is associated with Aspergillus flavus, not Pneumocystis.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man 6 weeks post-lung transplant develops fever and pulmonary nodules. Chest CT shows a nodule with a cavity and an intracavitary mass separated by a crescent of air. Which radiographic sign is being described?

explanation.summary: Late cavitation with a crescent of air around the necrotic fungal mass = air-crescent sign of invasive aspergillosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In invasive aspergillosis, early disease shows the halo sign (nodule with ground-glass rim). As infection progresses and neutrophils recover, central necrosis cavitates, producing the air-crescent sign.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Halo sign refers to ground-glass opacity surrounding a nodule (early finding), not a crescent of air.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tree-in-bud reflects small airway infections such as mycobacteria or viral bronchiolitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reverse halo (atoll sign) suggests organizing pneumonia or cryptogenic organizing pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Signet ring describes bronchiectasis with adjacent pulmonary artery, unrelated.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman with acute leukemia in prolonged neutropenia develops fever unresponsive to broad-spectrum antibiotics. Blood cultures are negative. Chest CT shows bilateral nodules with halo sign. Serum galactomannan returns positive. Which antifungal is the first-line treatment?

explanation.summary: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis first-line therapy is voriconazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: Voriconazole is preferred for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis due to strong activity against Aspergillus and excellent tissue penetration including CNS. Amphotericin B and isavuconazole are alternatives.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amphotericin B is second-line for invasive aspergillosis; voriconazole is preferred.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluconazole lacks activity against Aspergillus species.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TMP-SMX treats Pneumocystis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nystatin is a topical antifungal used for mucocutaneous Candida.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old HIV-positive man with CD4 count 30 cells/uL presents with PCP. Which laboratory marker, although non-specific, is elevated and supports fungal etiology given its cell wall component?

explanation.summary: Beta-D-glucan is a fungal cell wall component elevated in PCP but not specific to Pneumocystis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beta-D-glucan is a cell wall component present in most fungi including Pneumocystis. It supports the diagnosis of PCP (sensitivity ~92%, specificity ~86%) but is not specific and should be paired with staining/PCR.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Galactomannan is specific for Aspergillus, not Pneumocystis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Procalcitonin typically rises in bacterial infection, not fungal pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcal antigen detects Cryptococcus neoformans, not Pneumocystis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aspergillus-specific IgG diagnoses chronic pulmonary aspergillosis, not PCP.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with longstanding asthma presents with nasal obstruction, facial pressure, and decreased olfaction. CT shows nasal polyposis with opacification of both maxillary sinuses and differential densities suggesting dense mucin within the sinuses. Which diagnosis is most likely?

explanation.summary: Nasal polyposis, sinus opacification, and hyperdense eosinophilic mucin in an atopic/asthmatic patient = AFRS.
explanation.whyCorrect: AFRS is a chronic allergic inflammation directed against colonizing fungi, typically in atopic patients. Hallmarks include nasal polyposis, sinus opacification with differential densities from eosinophilic mucin accumulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mucormycosis features acute necrosis, black eschar, and rapid angioinvasion, not chronic polyposis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acute bacterial sinusitis is typically short-lived without polyposis or hyperdense mucin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IPA affects lung parenchyma, not the sinuses.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GPA produces destructive granulomatous lesions, not eosinophilic polypoid sinusitis.

questions.stem: A clinician is comparing hyphal morphology of two mold pathogens. Organism 1 has broad, ribbon-like, non-septate hyphae with ~90 degree branching. Organism 2 has narrower, septate hyphae with ~45 degree branching. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Organism 1 is Aspergillus; organism 2 is Mucor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Organism 1 is Candida; organism 2 is Cryptococcus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Organism 1 is Mucor; organism 2 is Aspergillus

explanation.summary: Broad non-septate hyphae with 90-degree branching = Mucor; septate hyphae with 45-degree branching = Aspergillus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucorales produce broad ribbon-like non-septate hyphae with right-angle (90 degrees) branching. Aspergillus species produce narrower septate hyphae with acute-angle (~45 degrees) branching.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reversed; broad non-septate right-angle is Mucorales.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aspergillus hyphae are exclusively septate with acute-angle branching.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pneumocystis lives as trophozoites and cysts, not hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Candida forms pseudohyphae and Cryptococcus is a yeast; neither matches these morphologies.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with untreated HIV has a CD4 count of 40 cells/uL. He presents with headache, fever, and confusion. Lumbar puncture shows lymphocytic pleocytosis. India ink staining of CSF reveals encapsulated round organisms. Which organism is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Encapsulated yeast on India ink in CSF of advanced HIV = Cryptococcus neoformans.
explanation.whyCorrect: India ink staining of CSF highlights the polysaccharide capsule of Cryptococcus neoformans as a clear halo around the yeast cell. Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis is common in advanced HIV with CD4 <100.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pneumocystis causes pneumonia, not encapsulated meningitis findings on India ink.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aspergillus is a mold with septate hyphae, not an encapsulated yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucor is a non-septate mold, not a capsule-forming yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida is a budding yeast with pseudohyphae but lacks a polysaccharide capsule demonstrable by India ink.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man with asthma and ABPA is diagnosed and started on treatment. Which pairing best reflects first-line therapy with an adjunct aimed at reducing fungal burden?

explanation.summary: ABPA: systemic corticosteroids are first-line; antifungals (itraconazole/voriconazole) reduce fungal burden.
explanation.whyCorrect: ABPA is an immune-mediated disease. Corticosteroids address the inflammatory hypersensitivity reaction, and antifungals such as itraconazole or voriconazole are added to reduce airway fungal burden.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Surgery is used for aspergilloma, not ABPA.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Amphotericin B is not standard ABPA therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TMP-SMX/pentamidine treat Pneumocystis, not ABPA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Caspofungin/fluconazole are not used as first-line for ABPA.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes presents with fever, hemoptysis, and a rapidly progressive pulmonary infiltrate over 5 days. Biopsy shows broad non-septate hyphae invading pulmonary vessels. Which statement best explains the clinical course?

explanation.summary: Pulmonary mucormycosis: angioinvasion -> thrombosis -> ischemic necrosis -> rapid progression with mortality 50-80%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucorales are angioinvasive and penetrate tissue barriers rapidly, occluding blood vessels and causing ischemic necrosis. This explains fulminant progression with hemoptysis and very high mortality.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Slow colonization characterizes CPA/aspergilloma, not Mucorales.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgE airway hyperreactivity describes ABPA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Granulomatous/immune complex pathology describes hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mucorales are not primarily intracellular organisms.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man with asthma has clinical and laboratory findings consistent with ABPA. Which laboratory test pattern best supports the diagnosis?

explanation.summary: ABPA: eosinophilia, elevated total serum IgE, and positive Aspergillus-specific IgE and IgG antibodies.
explanation.whyCorrect: ABPA is a Th2-driven hypersensitivity response. Classic labs include peripheral eosinophilia, markedly elevated total IgE, and positive Aspergillus-specific IgE and IgG antibodies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Galactomannan supports invasive aspergillosis, not ABPA.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta-D-glucan is not specific and does not establish ABPA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isolated Aspergillus IgG supports CPA/aspergilloma; ABPA also requires IgE and eosinophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ABPA is defined by elevated IgE; IgM has no role.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man with AML has suspected invasive aspergillosis. Bronchoalveolar lavage is sent for testing. Which combination most strongly supports a presumptive diagnosis when invasive tissue biopsy is not feasible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Positive BAL galactomannan plus BAL PCR for Aspergillus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Positive cryptococcal antigen plus India ink

choices.label: D
choices.text: Positive beta-D-glucan plus silver stain cysts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Positive acid-fast bacilli plus interferon-gamma release

explanation.summary: BAL galactomannan plus BAL PCR provides presumptive diagnosis of invasive aspergillosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the right clinical context, a positive BAL galactomannan, BAL PCR for Aspergillus, or positive serum galactomannan can establish a presumptive diagnosis of invasive aspergillosis when biopsy is not possible.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IgE and eosinophilia support ABPA, not invasive disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcal antigen and India ink diagnose cryptococcosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Beta-D-glucan plus silver cysts supports PCP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: AFB and IGRA diagnose tuberculosis, not aspergillosis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man develops severe PCP while on high-dose glucocorticoids for polymyositis. He has a documented severe sulfa allergy with prior Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Which of the following is the most appropriate alternative therapy?

explanation.summary: PCP second-line therapy for sulfa-allergic patients includes pentamidine, atovaquone, or clindamycin + primaquine.
explanation.whyCorrect: TMP-SMX is first-line for PCP. In patients with severe sulfa allergy, alternatives include pentamidine, atovaquone, or clindamycin plus primaquine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Voriconazole treats Aspergillus, not Pneumocystis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Amphotericin B has no role in PCP treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Caspofungin has limited activity against Pneumocystis and is not standard second-line therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Itraconazole treats CPA/ABPA, not PCP.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man from Wisconsin presents with a 3-week history of cough, pleuritic chest pain, and weight loss. He recently spent weeks hiking near rivers and forests. Chest X-ray shows a mass-like infiltrate. Sputum shows large, thick-walled yeast with broad-based budding. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

explanation.summary: Blastomyces dermatitidis is endemic to the Great Lakes and eastern US. The yeast form shows large, thick-walled cells with broad-based budding, distinguishing it from Histoplasma (narrow-based budding).
explanation.whyCorrect: The Wisconsin travel history (Great Lakes region), mass-like infiltrate, and large thick-walled yeast with broad-based budding are classic for Blastomyces dermatitidis. Broad-based budding is the key morphologic feature distinguishing Blastomyces from Histoplasma (narrow-based budding).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma shows small ovoid yeast with narrow-based budding that survive inside macrophages. The broad-based budding described here identifies Blastomyces.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides forms spherules filled with endospores in tissue, not yeast with broad-based budding. It is endemic to the arid southwestern US, not Wisconsin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus is a yeast with a very large prominent capsule (visualized with India ink). It does not show broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aspergillus is a mold (septate hyphae with acute-angle branching), not a yeast with broad-based budding.

questions.stem: A spelunker (cave explorer) from the Ohio River Valley develops fever, malaise, cough, and hilar lymphadenopathy. Sputum stain shows small ovoid yeast within macrophages. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

explanation.summary: Histoplasma capsulatum thrives in soil enriched with bird or bat droppings (caves). It is endemic to the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys. The yeast form is small, ovoid, with narrow-based budding, often found inside macrophages.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histoplasma lives in soil enriched with bird or bat droppings, making cave explorers (spelunkers) at increased risk. It is endemic to the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys. After inhalation, Histoplasma is phagocytized by lung macrophages, where it replicates intracellularly. The yeast form shows small ovoid yeast with narrow-based budding within macrophages.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces shows large, thick-walled yeast with broad-based budding. The small intracellular yeast with narrow-based budding identifies Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides forms spherules with endospores in tissue and is endemic to the arid southwest, not the Ohio River Valley.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus is an encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings, not bat droppings. It does not classically reside within macrophages on routine staining.
whyWrongByChoice.E: P. jirovecii shows indented, helmet-shaped cysts on silver stain. It occurs in severely immunocompromised patients (CD4 <200), not healthy spelunkers.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man from Arizona presents with fever, dry cough, and painful red nodules on his shins (erythema nodosum) after exposure to dry, dusty soil. Tissue biopsy shows large spherules filled with endospores. Which of the following is the causative organism?

explanation.summary: Coccidioides immitis causes Valley fever, endemic to the arid southwestern US (Arizona, California). In tissue at 37Â°C, it forms large spherules filled with endospores. Erythema nodosum is a common immune reaction to circulating fungal antigens.
explanation.whyCorrect: Coccidioides is endemic to the arid desert regions of the southwestern US. Exposure to dry, dusty soil is a risk factor. In tissue at 37Â°C, Coccidioides forms large spherules filled with endospores rather than typical yeastâ€”a unique morphologic feature. Erythema nodosum (painful red nodules on shins) is a common immune-mediated reaction to circulating fungal antigens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma shows small intracellular yeast with narrow-based budding, not spherules with endospores. It is endemic to the Ohio/Mississippi River valleys.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces shows large yeast with broad-based budding, not spherules. It is endemic to the Great Lakes/eastern US.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus is an encapsulated yeast without a mold form. It does not form spherules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paracoccidioides is endemic to South and Central America, not Arizona. Its yeast form shows multiple narrow-based buds (Captain's wheel), not spherules.

questions.stem: An HIV-positive man with CD4 count of 50 cells/mmÂ³ presents with fever, headache, and nuchal rigidity. CSF analysis shows an encapsulated yeast. Which of the following staining methods historically was used to visualize this organism?

explanation.summary: Cryptococcus neoformans has a prominent polysaccharide capsule that was historically visualized with India ink in CSF. India ink reveals a clear halo around the yeast cells. CrAg testing has largely replaced India ink.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcus neoformans has a very large, prominent polysaccharide capsule. Historically, India ink was used to visualize this capsule in CSFâ€”the ink particles cannot penetrate the capsule, creating a clear halo around the yeast. However, India ink has largely been replaced by the more sensitive and specific Cryptococcal Antigen (CrAg) test for rapid diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ziehl-Neelsen stain is the acid-fast stain for mycobacteria (TB), not Cryptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Standard Gram stain does not reliably visualize Cryptococcus's capsule. India ink or CrAg testing is needed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Silver stain (methenamine silver) is used for P. jirovecii and Aspergillus, not for visualizing Cryptococcus capsule.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Giemsa stain is used for blood parasites and some intracellular organisms, not for demonstrating the Cryptococcus capsule.

questions.stem: Histoplasma, Blastomyces, and Coccidioides are thermally dimorphic fungi. Which of the following correctly describes their morphology at body temperature (37Â°C) versus environmental temperature (25Â°C)?

explanation.summary: Thermally dimorphic fungi follow the rule 'mold in the cold (25Â°C), yeast in the heat (37Â°C).' At environmental temperatures they grow as molds; at body temperature they convert to yeast (or spherules in Coccidioides).
explanation.whyCorrect: Thermally dimorphic fungi follow the classic rule: 'mold in the cold (25Â°C), yeast in the heat (37Â°C).' At environmental temperatures, they grow in mold form; at body temperature, they convert to pathogenic yeast form (or spherules in the case of Coccidioides). This dimorphism is demonstrated in the lab by growing on Sabouraud agar at both temperatures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This reverses the relationship. Dimorphic fungi are molds at 25Â°C (environmental) and yeast at 37Â°C (body temperature).
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus spp. exist as yeast at both temperatures, but the thermally dimorphic fungi (Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides) convert between mold and yeast forms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aspergillus exists only as mold at both temperatures. The thermally dimorphic fungi convert to yeast at body temperature.
whyWrongByChoice.E: While spores/conidia are produced at 25Â°C, the key dimorphism is between mold form (25Â°C) and yeast form (37Â°C).

questions.stem: Among the geographically defined mycoses, which organism is most associated with dissemination to the central nervous system, particularly causing meningitis in immunocompromised patients?

explanation.summary: While all endemic fungi can disseminate to the CNS, Cryptococcus spp. are the most likely to cause CNS infection, particularly meningitis/meningoencephalitis in immunocompromised patients (especially AIDS).
explanation.whyCorrect: While all the endemic fungi can potentially disseminate to the CNS, Cryptococcus spp. are the most likely to infect the CNS. Prior to antiretrovirals, Cryptococcus was a major cause of meningitis in AIDS patients. Presentation includes fever, nuchal rigidity, and altered mental status, though in severely immunocompromised patients, classic inflammation signs may be absent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma can disseminate to the CNS but does so less commonly than Cryptococcus. Its most common dissemination involves the reticuloendothelial system.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces disseminates most commonly to the skin (verrucous lesions), not the CNS. CNS involvement occurs in only about 1% of cases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides can cause CNS meningitis, especially in immunocompromised patients, but Cryptococcus is the classic CNS mycosis in immunocompromised patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paracoccidioides most commonly disseminates to mucosal surfaces (oral/nasal ulcers), skin, and lymph nodes, not primarily the CNS.

questions.stem: A patient from rural Brazil presents with chronic cough, weight loss, and multiple painful ulcerative lesions of the oral mucosa. Biopsy shows large yeast with multiple narrow-based buds arranged circumferentially (Captain's wheel). Which organism is most likely?

explanation.summary: Paracoccidioides is a dimorphic fungus endemic to South and Central America. Its yeast form shows multiple narrow-based buds arranged circumferentially around a central mother cell, called the Captain's or Mariner's wheel. Oral mucosal ulcers are characteristic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Paracoccidioides is endemic to South and Central America (especially Brazil), primarily affecting adult men. In chronic cases, mucosal involvement occurs in over 50% of cases, with the mouth being most frequently affected. The yeast form shows large, round cells with multiple buds arranged circumferentiallyâ€”the Captain's or Mariner's wheel appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma shows small yeast with narrow-based budding (single buds, not multiple circumferential buds). It is endemic to the Ohio/Mississippi River valleys.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces shows large yeast with broad-based budding (single bud), not the multiple circumferential buds of Paracoccidioides. Blastomyces skin lesions are verrucous, not oral ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides forms spherules with endospores, not yeast with multiple buds. It is endemic to the southwestern US.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus is an encapsulated yeast without multiple buds. It primarily causes meningitis, not oral ulcers.

questions.stem: Blastomycosis disseminates most commonly to which of the following sites?

explanation.summary: The most common site of dissemination of blastomycosis is the skin (18% of cases). The most characteristic cutaneous finding is a verrucous (wart-like) lesion with irregular borders, consistent with the species name B. dermatitidis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blastomycosis disseminates most commonly to the skin (18% of cases). The most characteristic cutaneous finding is a verrucous (wart-like) lesion with irregular borders. This makes sense with the species name Blastomyces dermatitidis. Other dissemination sites include bone (4%), genitourinary (2%), and CNS (1%).

whyWrongByChoice.A: CNS involvement occurs in only about 1% of blastomycosis cases, much less common than skin dissemination (18%).
whyWrongByChoice.C: Liver is not the most common site of blastomycosis dissemination. It is more commonly a site for disseminated histoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Heart involvement is not a common site of blastomycosis dissemination.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Kidney is not the most common dissemination site. Genitourinary involvement occurs in about 2% of cases, compared to 18% for skin.

questions.stem: An immunocompromised patient from an endemic area has suspected Histoplasma infection. Which of the following rapid diagnostic tests can detect Histoplasma antigen in urine or serum?

explanation.summary: Histoplasma has galactomannan antigen that can be detected in urine and serum by antigen detection assays. However, galactomannan cross-reacts with Aspergillus and cannot distinguish between the two.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histoplasma can be diagnosed by urine and serum galactomannan antigen detection. Both Histoplasma and Aspergillus spp. have galactomannan, so this test cannot distinguish between the two. However, in the right clinical context (endemic area exposure, risk factors), a positive galactomannan helps confirm Histoplasma infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CrAg test detects Cryptococcus capsular antigen in serum or CSF, not Histoplasma antigen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Î²-D-glucan is a nonspecific fungal marker found in most fungi. While it can support a fungal infection diagnosis, it does not specifically identify Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: India ink is used to visualize the Cryptococcus capsule in CSF, not for Histoplasma detection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: While PCR can detect fungal DNA, galactomannan antigen testing is the specific rapid antigen test for Histoplasma.

questions.stem: For mild to moderate pulmonary histoplasmosis requiring treatment, which of the following is the first-line antifungal?

explanation.summary: Itraconazole is first-line for mild to moderate pulmonary histoplasmosis. Amphotericin B is reserved for severe or disseminated disease. Many mild infections are self-limited and may not require treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Itraconazole is the first-line antifungal for mild to moderate pulmonary histoplasmosis (and also for mild to moderate blastomycosis). It has good oral bioavailability and effectiveness against dimorphic fungi. Amphotericin B is reserved for severe or disseminated disease due to its rapid fungicidal activity but significant toxicity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amphotericin B is reserved for severe or disseminated histoplasmosis. For mild to moderate disease, itraconazole is preferred due to its better tolerability.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluconazole is a second-line agent for histoplasmosis and is first-line for coccidioidomycosis. Itraconazole is preferred for histoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole is first-line for invasive aspergillosis, not histoplasmosis. Itraconazole is preferred for endemic mycoses.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Caspofungin (echinocandin) is not standard treatment for histoplasmosis. It has limited activity against dimorphic fungi.

questions.stem: Cryptococcus neoformans has a different geographic distribution in the US compared to the other endemic fungi. Which of the following best describes its distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Restricted to the Ohio River Valley

choices.label: B
choices.text: Found only in the southwestern deserts

explanation.summary: Unlike the other geographically restricted endemic fungi, C. neoformans has nationwide distribution in the US. C. gattii is predominantly found on the west coast. C. neoformans is associated with pigeon droppings.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcus neoformans has nationwide distribution in the US and is not geographically restricted like the other endemic fungi. It is associated with pigeon droppings. In contrast, C. gattii is predominantly found in the Pacific Northwest. Histoplasma is in the Ohio/Mississippi River valleys, Blastomyces in the Great Lakes/eastern US, and Coccidioides in the arid southwest.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Ohio River Valley is the endemic region for Histoplasma, not Cryptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The southwestern deserts are endemic for Coccidioides (Valley fever), not Cryptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Pacific Northwest is where C. gattii is found, not C. neoformans. C. neoformans is found nationwide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. neoformans is found worldwide, not only in South America. Paracoccidioides is the fungus endemic to South America.

questions.stem: Histoplasma capsulatum can establish latent infection similar to Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Which of the following best explains the mechanism of latent Histoplasma infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The organism forms spores in the bloodstream

choices.label: C
choices.text: It encysts in the pleural space

choices.label: D
choices.text: It integrates DNA into host cell genomes

choices.label: E
choices.text: It becomes resistant to all antifungals

explanation.summary: Like M. tuberculosis, Histoplasma can survive within macrophages and persist in the lungs for decades without causing symptoms. Reactivation can occur years later with immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Similar to M. tuberculosis, Histoplasma capsulatum can survive within macrophages and persist in the lungs for decades without causing symptoms (latent infection). Initial exposure may be asymptomatic or cause only mild illness. Anyone with prior residence or travel in an endemic area remains at lifelong risk for reactivation, which most often occurs when immunosuppression develops.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma does not form spores in the bloodstream. It persists as yeast within macrophages in the lungs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Histoplasma does not encyst in the pleural space. It survives intracellularly within macrophages.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma does not integrate DNA into host genomes. This is a mechanism of some viruses (retroviruses), not fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Latency is not due to antifungal resistance. It is due to the organism's ability to survive within macrophages in an immunologically contained state.

questions.stem: For severe or disseminated disease caused by any of the geographically defined mycoses (Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides, or Cryptococcus), which of the following is the first-line antifungal?

explanation.summary: Amphotericin B is first-line for severe or disseminated disease caused by all the geographically defined mycoses. It provides rapid fungicidal activity and a broad antifungal spectrum, though toxicity limits its use to severe cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amphotericin B is the first-line treatment for severe or disseminated disease caused by any of the endemic mycoses (Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Cryptococcus). It provides rapid fungicidal activity by binding ergosterol in fungal membranes, creating pores. For Cryptococcal meningitis, flucytosine is added to amphotericin B. Azoles are used for mild-moderate disease and as step-down maintenance therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Itraconazole is first-line for mild-moderate histoplasmosis and blastomycosis but is insufficient for severe or disseminated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluconazole is first-line for mild-moderate coccidioidomycosis and serves as maintenance therapy, but not for initial treatment of severe disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole is first-line for invasive aspergillosis but is not the standard for severe endemic mycoses.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Terbinafine is used for dermatophyte infections (skin, nail fungus) and has no role in treating severe endemic mycoses.

questions.stem: Coccidioides is distinguished from other endemic fungi by its risk factor profile. Exposure to which of the following environmental conditions is specifically associated with coccidioidomycosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bird or bat droppings in caves

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dry, arid soil or fine silt

choices.label: E
choices.text: Decaying plant material in tropical regions

explanation.summary: Coccidioides is found in dry, arid soil of the southwestern US. Exposure to dry soil or fine silt (e.g., during dust storms, construction, or farming) is the specific risk factor. There is no association with bird or bat droppings.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike Histoplasma (bird/bat droppings) and Cryptococcus (pigeon droppings), Coccidioides is specifically associated with exposure to dry, arid soil or fine silt in endemic regions (Arizona, California's Central Valley). There is no association with animal droppings. Inhalation of arthroconidia from disturbed soil causes infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bird or bat droppings in caves are associated with Histoplasma, not Coccidioides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pigeon droppings are associated with Cryptococcus neoformans, not Coccidioides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: River and forest environments are more associated with Blastomyces and Histoplasma in the Great Lakes/eastern US, not the arid conditions linked to Coccidioides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Decaying plant material in tropical regions is associated with various fungi, including Cryptococcus gattii, not the arid-soil-associated Coccidioides.

questions.stem: Which of the following geographically defined fungi is NOT thermally dimorphic and exists only as a yeast?

explanation.summary: Cryptococcus spp. are considered yeasts without a clear mold form and are thus not thermally dimorphic. All other listed fungi (Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Paracoccidioides) are thermally dimorphic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcus spp. exist only as yeast and do not have a mold form, making them the exception among the geographically defined mycoses. They are not thermally dimorphic. Histoplasma, Blastomyces, and Coccidioides all follow the 'mold in the cold, yeast in the heat' pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma is thermally dimorphic: mold at 25Â°C with micro/macroconidia; yeast at 37Â°C with narrow-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces is thermally dimorphic: mold at 25Â°C with microconidia; yeast at 37Â°C with broad-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides is thermally dimorphic: mold at 25Â°C with arthroconidia; spherules with endospores at 37Â°C.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paracoccidioides is thermally dimorphic: mold in the environment; yeast with multiple buds (Captain's wheel) in tissue.

questions.stem: Histoplasma capsulatum can form caseating granulomas on pathologic examination, similar to which of the following infectious diseases?

explanation.summary: Histoplasma infection can produce caseating granulomas, similar to M. tuberculosis. Both organisms cause intracellular infection in macrophages and stimulate Th1 cell-mediated immune responses that form granulomas.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pathologic evaluation of histoplasmosis may demonstrate caseating granulomas, similar to tuberculosis. Both Histoplasma and M. tuberculosis are intracellular pathogens that replicate within macrophages and stimulate Th1/IFN-Î³-driven immune responses that form granulomas. The clinical presentation can also mimic TB with nodular infiltrates and cavitation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sarcoidosis causes noncaseating granulomas (without central necrosis), not caseating granulomas like Histoplasma and TB.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aspergillosis causes tissue invasion by hyphae and tissue necrosis but does not typically form the caseating granulomas seen with Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PCP causes alveolar filling with a foamy eosinophilic exudate, not granuloma formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Legionnaires' disease causes acute pneumonia without granuloma formation.

questions.stem: For mild to moderate pulmonary coccidioidomycosis (Valley fever) requiring treatment, which of the following is the first-line antifungal?

explanation.summary: Fluconazole is first-line for mild to moderate coccidioidomycosis. This differs from histoplasmosis and blastomycosis, where itraconazole is first-line. Many mild Coccidioides infections are self-limited.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fluconazole is the first-line antifungal for mild to moderate coccidioidomycosis. This is a notable difference from histoplasmosis and blastomycosis, where itraconazole is preferred. Many Valley fever infections are mild or self-limited but may require therapy in high-risk patients. Itraconazole is a second-line alternative for coccidioidomycosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Itraconazole is second-line for coccidioidomycosis (but first-line for histoplasmosis and blastomycosis). Fluconazole is preferred for Coccidioides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amphotericin B is reserved for severe or disseminated coccidioidomycosis, not mild-moderate disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole is first-line for invasive aspergillosis, not coccidioidomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Caspofungin is not standard treatment for coccidioidomycosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following rapid antigen tests is most sensitive for diagnosing Cryptococcus infection in CSF?

explanation.summary: The Cryptococcal Antigen (CrAg) test detects capsular polysaccharide in serum or CSF and is very sensitive for Cryptococcus infection. It has replaced India ink as the standard diagnostic test.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Cryptococcal Antigen (CrAg) test detects the polysaccharide capsular antigen of Cryptococcus in serum or CSF. It is very sensitive and has largely replaced India ink staining as the standard diagnostic method. CrAg can be detected even in severely immunocompromised patients who may have atypical presentations without classic meningeal signs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Galactomannan antigen testing detects Aspergillus and Histoplasma antigens, not Cryptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Î²-D-glucan is a nonspecific marker for most fungal infections. Cryptococcus does not possess significant amounts of Î²-D-glucan, making this test less useful.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aspergillus-specific IgE is used for ABPA diagnosis, not Cryptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Histoplasma urine antigen detects Histoplasma galactomannan, not Cryptococcus.

questions.stem: Erythema nodosum can occur as an immune reaction in patients with coccidioidomycosis. Which of the following best describes this phenomenon?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct fungal invasion of the skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immune reaction to circulating fungal antigens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Allergic contact dermatitis to soil exposure

explanation.summary: Erythema nodosum in coccidioidomycosis is not due to fungal dissemination to the skin but rather an immune-mediated reaction to circulating fungal antigens leaking from the infection site into the blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Erythema nodosum (painful red nodules, usually on the shins) in coccidioidomycosis is not caused by direct fungal dissemination to the skin. Instead, it is an immune system reaction to fungal antigens circulating in the blood from the pulmonary infection site. This presentation is not unique to coccidioidomycosis and can occur with other fungal infections and non-infectious causes (e.g., Crohn's disease, sarcoidosis).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Erythema nodosum is not due to direct fungal invasion of the skin. It is an immune-mediated reaction, not infectious skin involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Allergic contact dermatitis is a localized skin reaction to external allergens, not the systemic immune response seen with erythema nodosum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Erythema nodosum occurs as part of the immune response to the infection, not as a drug reaction. It can occur before treatment is started.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Erythema nodosum is not a bacterial skin infection. It is an immune-mediated inflammatory condition of the subcutaneous fat.

questions.stem: Immunocompromised patients with endemic mycoses often have absent or poorly formed granulomas on pathology. Which arm of the immune system is required for effective granuloma formation?

explanation.summary: Effective granuloma formation requires a strong Th1 cell-mediated immune response, especially IFN-Î³-activated macrophages. Immunocompromised patients (HIV/AIDS, corticosteroids, transplant) cannot mount this organized response.
explanation.whyCorrect: Effective granuloma formation requires a strong Th1 cell-mediated immune response, especially IFN-Î³-activated macrophages. When patients are immunocompromised (advanced HIV/AIDS, corticosteroid use, transplant immunosuppression, chemotherapy), they cannot mount this organized response. Instead of granulomas, pathology shows diffuse organisms with minimal granulomatous inflammation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Humoral immunity (antibodies) is not the primary driver of granuloma formation. Granulomas require T cell-mediated (Th1) immunity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complement activation aids in innate immune defense but does not drive granuloma formation, which requires adaptive Th1 responses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IgE-mediated responses are involved in allergic conditions (like ABPA) and parasitic immunity, not granuloma formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neutrophil oxidative burst is important for killing organisms like Aspergillus but is not the mechanism of granuloma formation.

questions.stem: Chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis with cavitation can mimic which of the following conditions, especially in smokers?

explanation.summary: Chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis with progressive cavitation and adenopathy can mimic both tuberculosis and lung cancer. Smokers are at risk for both CPH and cancer, making differentiation particularly important.
explanation.whyCorrect: As chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis progresses, nodules can cavitate and cause adenopathy, mimicking both tuberculosis and lung cancer. Smokers are at risk for both CPH and cancer, making this differential particularly challenging. Cancer should always be considered on the differential in patients with cavitary lung lesions and risk factors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asthma causes airway obstruction with wheezing, not cavitary lung lesions. ABPA can complicate asthma but is different from chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Heart failure causes pulmonary edema and pleural effusions, not cavitary lung lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pulmonary embolism causes perfusion defects and possible infarction, not chronic cavitary disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pneumothorax is air in the pleural space causing lung collapse, not a chronic cavitary process.

questions.stem: For cryptococcal meningitis in an immunocompromised patient, which of the following drug combinations is the standard initial (induction) therapy?

explanation.summary: Cryptococcal meningitis is treated with induction therapy of amphotericin B plus flucytosine, followed by maintenance with fluconazole. Flucytosine provides synergistic fungicidal activity and good CNS penetration.
explanation.whyCorrect: For severe/disseminated cryptococcal infection including meningitis, the standard induction therapy is amphotericin B plus flucytosine (5-FC). Flucytosine adds synergistic fungicidal activity and has excellent CNS penetration. After induction, patients are stepped down to fluconazole for long-term maintenance therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Itraconazole plus fluconazole is not the standard induction regimen for cryptococcal meningitis. Amphotericin B with flucytosine is needed for the aggressive initial treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Voriconazole plus caspofungin is not standard for cryptococcal meningitis. This combination might be used for aspergillosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TMP-SMX plus doxycycline treats Nocardia and Q fever respectively, not cryptococcal meningitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fluconazole monotherapy is used for maintenance (consolidation) therapy after induction, not as initial treatment for cryptococcal meningitis.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old spelunker in Ohio develops fever, cough, and malaise 10 days after exploring a cave heavily populated by bats. Chest CT shows nodular pneumonia with mediastinal lymphadenopathy resembling miliary TB. Lung biopsy reveals caseating granulomas with small ovoid yeast inside macrophages exhibiting narrow-based budding. Which organism is responsible?

explanation.summary: Histoplasma: caves/bat droppings, intracellular yeast in macrophages, narrow-based budding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ohio River valley, bat exposure, and small intracellular yeast with narrow-based budding are pathognomonic for Histoplasma capsulatum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blastomyces shows broad-based budding and is not intracellular.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides forms spherules, not intracellular yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus is a large encapsulated yeast, not intracellular.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paracoccidioides is endemic to Latin America with captain's wheel morphology.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old forestry worker from Wisconsin develops subacute pneumonia with productive cough and a verrucous skin lesion on his forearm. Sputum KOH prep reveals large, thick-walled yeast with broad-based budding. Which is the most appropriate first-line therapy?

explanation.summary: Mild-moderate blastomycosis: itraconazole first-line.
explanation.whyCorrect: Broad-based budding yeast from the Great Lakes region with mild-to-moderate disease is blastomycosis; itraconazole is first-line.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amphotericin B is reserved for severe/disseminated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluconazole is second-line for blastomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole is not first-line for blastomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Flucytosine is adjunctive for cryptococcal infection, not blastomycosis.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old construction worker in Arizona's Central Valley develops fever, dry cough, pleuritic chest pain, and painful red nodules on his shins 2 weeks after working in dusty soil. Biopsy of a pulmonary nodule shows large structures filled with small endospores. Which is the most likely organism?

explanation.summary: Valley fever with spherules and erythema nodosum indicates Coccidioides.
explanation.whyCorrect: SW US desert dust exposure with spherule-endospore morphology and erythema nodosum is classic for Coccidioides.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma does not form spherules; associated with bat/bird droppings.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces forms broad-based budding yeast, not spherules.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus gattii is an encapsulated yeast in the Pacific Northwest.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paracoccidioides is in Latin America and forms captain's wheel.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old Brazilian agricultural worker who recently immigrated to the US presents with 2 months of productive cough, weight loss, and painful ulcerative lesions on the oral mucosa. Biopsy shows large yeast with multiple narrow-based buds arranged circumferentially around a central mother cell. Which organism is responsible?

explanation.summary: Captain's wheel yeast with oral mucosal lesions in a Latin American patient = Paracoccidioides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Paracoccidioides is endemic to Latin America, commonly involves oral mucosa, and has the pathognomonic captain's/mariner's wheel morphology.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces shows single broad-based budding, not multiple buds.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Histoplasma is small intracellular yeast with single narrow-based budding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coccidioides forms spherules, not budding yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cryptococcus is a single encapsulated yeast without multiple buds.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with AIDS (CD4 25) presents with fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and pancytopenia. He lived in Kentucky as a child. Bone marrow biopsy shows diffuse small intracellular organisms with minimal granuloma formation. Which factor best explains the poorly formed granulomas?

explanation.summary: Granuloma formation requires Th1/IFN-gamma-activated macrophages, impaired in AIDS.
explanation.whyCorrect: Effective granulomas need a strong Th1 cell-mediated response with IFN-gamma activation of macrophages; AIDS impairs this, producing diffuse organisms with minimal granulomatous inflammation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma lacks a prominent capsule.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophil burst defects relate to chronic granulomatous disease, not AIDS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Complement deficiency is not the cause of granuloma failure in AIDS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: B-cell/antibody function is largely preserved in AIDS; T-cell loss is the issue.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old smoker with COPD in Tennessee has 6 months of progressive cough, weight loss, and cavitary upper lobe lesions on CT. Sputum GMS stain reveals small intracellular yeast with narrow-based budding. Which complicating diagnosis should be most strongly considered?

explanation.summary: Chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis in smokers: consider cancer on differential.
explanation.whyCorrect: The PDF specifically notes that cancer should be considered because smokers are at risk for both chronic pulmonary histoplasmosis and lung cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus is possible but not specifically highlighted in this context.
whyWrongByChoice.B: TB is on the differential but cancer is the specific concern noted for smokers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sarcoidosis does not fit the smoker/cavitary picture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PE does not produce cavitary upper lobe lesions.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with HIV/AIDS in Oklahoma presents with headache, fever, and altered mental status. LP shows elevated opening pressure and lymphocytic pleocytosis. India ink stain shows large yeast with a prominent capsule. Which test is most sensitive for diagnosis?

explanation.summary: CrAg is the most sensitive test for Cryptococcus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) test in serum or CSF is very sensitive and has largely replaced India ink for rapid diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Galactomannan detects Histoplasma/Aspergillus, not Cryptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta-D-glucan is nonspecific and Cryptococcus has low levels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunodiffusion is used for Coccidioides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chocolate agar is for Haemophilus, not fungi.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old AIDS patient has severe disseminated cryptococcal meningitis. Which regimen is most appropriate for initial induction therapy?

explanation.summary: Severe Cryptococcus: amphotericin B + flucytosine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the table, severe/disseminated cryptococcal disease requires amphotericin B; flucytosine is added specifically for Cryptococcus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Itraconazole is not first-line for severe cryptococcal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluconazole alone is maintenance therapy, not induction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole/caspofungin are not the standard cryptococcal induction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Posaconazole is not standard induction therapy.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has suspected fungal pneumonia. Urine galactomannan antigen returns positive. Which pair of organisms can this assay NOT distinguish between?

explanation.summary: Galactomannan is shared by Histoplasma and Aspergillus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both Histoplasma and Aspergillus possess galactomannan antigen, so the assay cannot distinguish them. Candida, Blastomyces, Coccidioides, and Cryptococcus do not have galactomannan.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Neither Blastomyces nor Coccidioides has galactomannan.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither Cryptococcus nor Candida has galactomannan.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus lacks galactomannan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida lacks galactomannan.

questions.stem: A sputum specimen is cultured on Sabouraud agar at 25°C and grows septate hyphae forming barrel-shaped arthroconidia. At 37°C, tissue biopsy shows large sac-like structures filled with small endospores rather than budding yeast. Which geographic exposure fits best?

explanation.summary: Arthroconidia and spherules = Coccidioides = SW US desert.
explanation.whyCorrect: Coccidioides forms arthroconidia in mold phase and spherules filled with endospores in tissue; endemic to arid SW US including Arizona.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mississippi caves suggest Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Great Lakes forests suggest Blastomyces.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pacific NW decaying wood suggests C. gattii.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Brazil suggests Paracoccidioides.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man in Washington state develops cough and mental status changes. MRI shows multiple pulmonary and cerebral nodular lesions (cryptococcomas). He has no immunocompromise. Which organism is most consistent with this presentation?

explanation.summary: Pacific Northwest + immunocompetent host + cryptococcomas = C. gattii.
explanation.whyCorrect: C. gattii is predominantly found in the Pacific Northwest and notably infects immunocompetent hosts, producing cryptococcomas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. neoformans is nationwide and typically affects immunocompromised patients (pigeon droppings).
whyWrongByChoice.C: Blastomyces is endemic to the east, not PNW.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Histoplasma is endemic to Ohio/Mississippi valleys.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Coccidioides is in SW desert regions.

questions.stem: A patient with suspected fungal pneumonia has a urine antigen test positive for Blastomyces. The lab cautions that this result may not be definitive. Which organism most commonly cross-reacts with this assay?

explanation.summary: Blastomyces urine antigen cross-reacts with Histoplasma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The PDF explicitly notes cross-reactivity of the Blastomyces urine antigen test with Histoplasma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Coccidioides is detected by serum/CSF immunodiffusion without this cross-reactivity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptococcus is detected by CrAg without cross-reactivity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aspergillus shares galactomannan with Histoplasma, not Blastomyces.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida does not share this cross-reactivity.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man who lived in Ohio 20 years ago and now lives in New York begins chemotherapy for lymphoma. He develops fever, pancytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly. Urine antigen is positive for Histoplasma. Which best explains his infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recent acute exposure in New York

explanation.summary: Histoplasma establishes latency; reactivation occurs with immunosuppression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Like TB, Histoplasma can persist in macrophages for decades and reactivate when immunosuppression develops (e.g., chemotherapy).

whyWrongByChoice.A: NY is not endemic for Histoplasma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Contamination does not explain the clinical syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cross-reactivity doesn't explain clinical disseminated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chemotherapy immunosuppression is the inciting factor, not congenital immunodeficiency.

questions.stem: A mold form of a dimorphic fungus shows septate hyphae bearing BOTH microconidia and large tuberculated sun-shaped macroconidia on Sabouraud agar at 25°C. Which organism is this?

explanation.summary: Sun-shaped macroconidia are characteristic of Histoplasma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histoplasma mold has both microconidia and large sun-shaped (tuberculated) macroconidia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces mold has only microconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides mold produces arthroconidia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryptococcus is not thermally dimorphic and has no mold form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paracoccidioides mold does not show these sun-shaped macroconidia.

questions.stem: A patient with pulmonary disease has a fungal culture that does NOT exhibit thermal dimorphism on Sabouraud agar at 25°C vs 37°C. Which organism is most consistent?

explanation.summary: Cryptococcus is a yeast only, not thermally dimorphic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptococcus spp. are considered yeasts without a clear mold form and are not thermally dimorphic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histoplasma is thermally dimorphic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blastomyces is thermally dimorphic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coccidioides is dimorphic (mold with arthroconidia; spherules in tissue).
whyWrongByChoice.E: Paracoccidioides is thermally dimorphic.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old poultry farmer in Arkansas has mild self-limited pulmonary histoplasmosis with persistent mild symptoms for 3 weeks. He remains ambulatory and is otherwise healthy. Which is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?

explanation.summary: Mild-moderate histoplasmosis with persistent symptoms: itraconazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: Itraconazole is first-line for mild-to-moderate histoplasmosis; it is used for persistent symptoms or disseminated disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Persistent symptoms warrant treatment rather than observation only.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amphotericin B is reserved for severe disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole is not first-line for histoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Flucytosine is adjunctive for Cryptococcus.

questions.stem: A patient suspected of fungal CNS disease undergoes CSF antigen testing. Which assay is the recommended CSF test for identifying Coccidioides infection?

explanation.summary: Coccidioides: serum and CSF immunodiffusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the PDF, Coccidioides is identified via serum and CSF immunodiffusion assay.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Galactomannan is for Histoplasma/Aspergillus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta-D-glucan is not the specified test for Coccidioides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CrAg is for Cryptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urine antigen is for Histoplasma (and Blastomyces).

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man from Minnesota presents with subacute pneumonia and a verrucous cutaneous lesion with irregular borders on his forearm. Which is the most common site of dissemination for this organism?

explanation.summary: Blastomyces: skin is the most common site of dissemination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Skin involvement (verrucous lesions) is the most common extrapulmonary site for Blastomyces dermatitidis (~18%).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymph nodes are more classic for disseminated histoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CNS involvement is uncommon (~1%) for Blastomyces.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bone marrow dissemination is more typical of disseminated histoplasmosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral mucosal lesions are characteristic of Paracoccidioides.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with HIV (CD4 40) in California develops meningitis but has no fever or nuchal rigidity, only altered mental status. Which factor best explains the atypical presentation?

explanation.summary: Severely immunocompromised patients may lack classic inflammatory signs.
explanation.whyCorrect: In advanced AIDS, the inflammatory response is impaired so classic meningeal signs (fever, nuchal rigidity) may be absent; special attention is warranted to neurologic symptoms alone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No antibiotic pretreatment is described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: AIDS patients often have very high fungal burdens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Altered mental status is not an early feature alone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Host immune detection is intrinsically impaired, not evaded.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman with mild Valley fever (fever, dry cough) has a positive Coccidioides immunodiffusion and is otherwise healthy without dissemination. Which is the most appropriate first-line pharmacotherapy?

explanation.summary: Mild-moderate coccidioidomycosis: fluconazole first-line.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the treatment table, fluconazole is first-line for mild to moderate coccidioidomycosis; itraconazole is second-line.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Itraconazole is second-line for coccidioidomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amphotericin B is reserved for severe/disseminated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole is not first-line.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Echinocandins are not effective against Coccidioides.

questions.stem: A patient with Crohn's disease develops painful red nodular lesions on her shins. She has no travel history or fungal exposure. Which best describes the likely pathophysiology of the skin lesions?

explanation.summary: Erythema nodosum can arise from non-infectious causes like Crohn's, representing an immune reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Erythema nodosum is an immune-mediated reaction presenting as painful red nodules on the shins; it can occur from fungal antigens or non-infectious causes such as Crohn's disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No fungal exposure; this is not dissemination.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cellulitis is diffuse and unilateral, not bilateral shin nodules.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No infectious granuloma is present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: EN is septal panniculitis, not vasculitis with organism invasion.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old landscaper in Indiana develops severe disseminated blastomycosis with hypoxic respiratory failure and skin lesions. Which is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?

explanation.summary: Severe/disseminated blastomycosis: amphotericin B initial therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the treatment table, severe or disseminated blastomycosis (as well as histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis, and cryptococcosis) is treated with amphotericin B as initial therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Itraconazole is first-line only for mild-moderate disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluconazole is used for maintenance after amphotericin B.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Voriconazole is not standard for severe blastomycosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Posaconazole is not standard initial therapy.
